problems: MOST SERIOUS: invite_department_head stores the live single-use Department Head invitation link in plaintext. Request: SAO POST /api/ai/assistant/messages/180/action/confirm {"fields":{"college_id":"6"}}. Result: 200, and ai_messages id 180 content is 'The invitation link is ready... http://127.0.0.1:5173/accept-invitation?token=ruRl...' (also in payload.result.message). The invitation table stores only a hash, so this bypasses that. AskAiChatService::history() (lines 622-636) sends earlier completed messages' content to the language model on every later turn in the same conversation, so the secret would also be sent to the model once one is configured; it also stays readable in conversation history. Anyone who gets the link before the Department Head can accept it and become that college's head. Decide: keep the link out of the stored message (show it only in the confirm response, or have the SAO create it from the college page), or exclude action result messages from history and redact the token after display.

Minor: a card with no errors serializes 'errors' as [] (empty JSON array) in the chat response, but the contract says a map ({} or keyed by field). After a 422 it is a proper object. A client that tests Object.keys works either way, but the shape is inconsistent.

Minor: allow_applicant does not pre-fill the student even when the message names exactly one eligible student (value null; the card only lists that student first). The contract allows this, but the dean must still pick.

Minor: confirm and cancel share the throttle:ai-generation limit (5 per minute per user) with chat, so a person who asks and confirms several things quickly gets 429 'Too many requests' on a confirm. Specified in the report, but worth knowing; the card stays awaiting_confirmation so a retry works.

Minor: the create_task note says the body adds task_kind standalone, but the stored task has task_type 'regular' (the column is task_type, no task_kind). This is the real endpoint's value, so behaviour matches the form.

Environment note: all seeded students in the dean's college belong to an active student organization, so allow_applicant can't succeed on seed data alone. I added a test user (school_id 2199001) and account_profiles row to the live DB to prove the success path. Test records left in the dev DB: events 5, tasks 9, budgets 4, announcements 10 and 11, two grievances, applicant grant 1, college 6 with organization 12, department head invitation 1, user 2199001, and approval_requests 11 to 13. Nothing seeded was deleted.
